name: lpqi_spad64_i2cass_nextgen
label: LPQI IMSE-LPQI 64x64 SPAD array with microlenses (final: 10 ps, R = 10 000 spectrograph)
sources: F. Prada (LPQI PI), email to P. Nugent 2026-10-07: PDE 0.5 with microlenses, 6.7e6 cps capture ceiling

F. Prada, 2026-10-09 (via P. Nugent): the final LPQI instrument -- 10 ps timing, the 6.7e6 cps ceiling is PER PIXEL, and an R ~ 10 000 spectrograph over 400-950 nm feeds the array (spectrograph lpqi_r10000, backend lpqi_r10000_nextgen)
Quintana et al. 2026, Sensors 26, 5757: the published 64x64 array (lpqi_spad64_i2cass) this one extends
notes: The final LPQI detector: the microlensed IMSE-LPQI 64x64 SPAD array behind an R ~ 10 000 spectrograph (400-950 nm, ~8650 channels of lambda/10 000). Each spectral channel falls on its own pixel(s); n_pixels 4 is the pixels per channel (dead time and dark counts per channel).

max_cps_per_pixel 6.7e6: the capture ceiling is per pixel, so dispersed over ~8650 channels the array is never readout-limited on the LPQI targets; the filter backends (lpqi_nextgen_*) concentrate the star on 4 pixels and are limited above 2.7e7 cps.
PDE: 0.50 over 400-550 nm and 0.20 at 650 nm from F. Prada; the fall-off to 950 nm (0.15 at 700, 0.08 at 800, 0.04 at 900, 0.025 at 950) is an ASSUMED silicon-SPAD shape pending the measured curve.
10 ps FWHM timing (F. Prada 2026-10-09); at R = 10 000 the coherence time is ~0.2 ps, so the pair timing sets the g2 width.
assumptions: pde_table_nm beyond 650 nm (silicon-SPAD shape, scaled to the quoted 0.5)
